skill.name: performance-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze influencer campaigns against targets and benchmarks. Compare platforms, creators, content, engagement quality, sentiment, conversions, and attribution.
skill.summary: Turn influencer campaign data into scorecards, rankings, attributed outcomes, and prioritized recommendations.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown links, code fences, placeholders, and metadata URLs. However, SKILL.md line 58 directs execution of an out-of-package Python connector and use of environment-held API credentials. Publication should require connector review, explicit network consent, and documented credential handling.

remediation.issue: The YouTube workflow executes a Python connector that is not included in the audited skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle and audit the connector, or remove the command. Require explicit user approval before execution and network access.

remediation.issue: The YouTube workflow expects API credentials from the environment without describing secret handling.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact variable, minimum key permissions, destination API, and redaction rules. Never print or persist the key.

content.value_statement: Influencer results are difficult to compare across creators, platforms, and attribution methods. This skill converts campaign data into scorecards, rankings, insights, and recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Scores campaign metrics against supplied targets and benchmarks.
Ranks platforms, creators, content formats, and themes.
Analyzes engagement quality, comment sentiment, and purchase intent signals.
Maps conversions across promo codes, UTM links, direct attribution, and estimates.
Identifies winning content patterns and underperformance causes.
Produces prioritized learnings, roster decisions, and future campaign recommendations.
limitations: Requires campaign exports, screenshots, analytics, or metrics supplied by the user.
Cannot verify missing benchmarks, attribution assumptions, or creator-reported data.
Does not calculate complete dollar-level ROI or final C3 scores.
YouTube retrieval requires an external connector and API key not included here.

use_cases.title: Review a completed campaign
use_cases.description: Compare final results with targets and identify the strongest creators, platforms, and content.

use_cases.title: Optimize an active campaign
use_cases.description: Find early underperformance and decide where to adjust creators, formats, or platform allocation.

use_cases.title: Build reusable benchmarks
use_cases.description: Capture performance patterns and creator baselines for future planning and selection.

prompt_templates.title: Score one campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [campaign] using these results, targets, and benchmarks: [data]. Summarize performance and list the three most important actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with consolidated campaign data

prompt_templates.title: Compare creators
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [creator list] for [campaign]. Rank them by reach, engagement, conversions, and efficiency. Explain each renewal recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Find winning content
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these post-level results and comments: [data]. Compare formats, themes, hooks, sentiment, and purchase intent. Identify patterns worth testing again.

prompt_templates.title: Run a full attribution review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [campaign] across platforms and creators using [data]. Separate measured, user-provided, and estimated outcomes. Apply [significance criteria] before declaring winners.

output_examples.input: Campaign results with reach, engagement, conversions, targets, and platform totals.
output: Overall performance: Above target for reach and engagement, below target for conversions.
Top platform: TikTok produced the strongest engagement and conversion efficiency.
Priority action: Test stronger landing-page alignment before increasing spend.

output_examples.input: Post-level metrics and comments from five creators.
output: Top creator: @creator1 led qualified engagement and attributed sales.
Winning pattern: Short demonstrations with a direct opening generated more saves and purchase questions.
Roster decision: Renew two creators, keep one testing, and replace two underperformers.

output_examples.input: Promo-code, UTM, direct, and estimated conversion records.
output_examples.output: The analysis separates attribution methods, flags overlapping claims, and ranks recommendations by evidence strength.

best_practices: Label every metric as measured, user-provided, calculated, or estimated.
Supply campaign targets, comparison periods, and creator-level source data.
Apply statistical and practical thresholds before declaring a winner.
anti_patterns: Do not compare creators using totals when audience size and spend differ materially.
Do not combine promo, UTM, and estimated conversions without checking overlap.
Do not treat sentiment samples or screenshots as complete population data.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide campaign dates, creator posts, platform metrics, targets, benchmarks, traffic, conversions, sales, and attribution records when available.

faq.question: Can it compare creators across platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide comparable metrics and spend data. The skill can normalize context and explain platform differences.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: It can organize revenue and efficiency inputs, but complete dollar-level ROI belongs in the separate ROI calculator workflow.

faq.question: Can it retrieve live platform data?
faq.answer: The core workflow uses supplied data. YouTube retrieval needs an external Python connector and an API key.

faq.question: How does it handle missing benchmarks?
faq.answer: It should state the gap, use supplied historical comparisons when appropriate, and avoid unsupported performance claims.

faq.question: Can it analyze comment sentiment?
faq.answer: Yes. It can group supplied comments by sentiment and intent, but results depend on sample coverage and data quality.
